raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old Latinx male with known HIV, diagnosed 6 years prior and nonadherent with his ART for over 2 years presented to the emergency department with persistent fevers, bilateral flank pain, nausea, and vomiting for 5 days. Social history revealed a male who has sex with male both insertive and receptive and significant alcohol abuse. He denied any travel outside of the United States or exposure to any animals.
Upon further questioning, the patient revealed a similar constellation of symptoms of fever and abdominal pain 3 years ago, was found to have pancytopenia and generalized lymphadenopathy, and admitted to an outside facility. At that time, a left axillary lymph node biopsy was performed which revealed benign lymphoid hyperplasia with no malignancy and a right inguinal lymph node excisional biopsy that revealed fibroadipose tissue with focal lymphoid hyperplasia. Flow cytometry of the samples showed many lymphoid cells but no evidence of monoclonality in B cell population. A bone marrow biopsy showed slightly hypocellular marrow with no evidence of lymphoma or myelodysplastic syndrome. His symptoms improved after he became adherent to his ART.
Upon this presentation, vital signs were significant for a temperature of 38.8 C, blood pressure of 161/96 mm Hg, heart rate of 145 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute. Examination showed hepatosplenomegaly, and nontender axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy.
Laboratory work up revealed pancytopenia, high HIV viral load, elevated sedimentation rate, positive cytomegalovirus (CMV) immunoglobulin G (IgG) and ParvoB19 IgG, and negative CMV and Parvo B19 DNA polymerase chain reaction (Table 1). Patient was empirically started on broad spectrum antibiotics but continued to have fevers. A decision to discontinue antibiotics was made when all cultures continued to remain negative. Imagings were significant for bilateral diffuse axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly (Figures 1-4).
Differential diagnosis at this time remained very broad from infectious etiologies including viral, fungal, mycobacterial, or parasitic on one side, and AIDS-associated malignancies such as lymphoma on the other side.
His CD4 cell count came back as 27 cells/microL (6%) and HIV viral load of 98 200 copies/mL. HIV genotype results showed no transmissible resistance, so he was restarted on his previous ART regimen with Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir AF (Biktarvy).
Bone marrow biopsy and aspirate showed normocellular marrow with megakaryocytic hyperplasia, decreased iron, no evidence of acid-fast or fungal organisms, pancytopenia, and no evidence of parvovirus or malignancy. CT-guided right inguinal lymph node core biopsy resulted in scant fragments of lymphoid and fibrous tissue and was nondiagnostic.
His hospital course was complicated with clostridioides difficile colitis with diarrhea, which resolved with oral vancomycin therapy.
After a nonrevealing exhausting work up, the decision was made to perform a right inguinal excisional biopsy. Histopathology showed interfollicular plasma cells and germinal centers with vascularization and "onion-skin" hyaline vascular appearance. HHV-8 immunostaining showed presence of HHV-8 (Figures 5-7). Serum revealed an elevated level of HHV-8 of 2 288 277 copies/mL (nmL <1000). Therefore, a diagnosis of HHV-8-associated MCD was reached.
The patient was started on 6 cycle of rituximab chemotherapy and transitioned to outpatient therapy. He improved clinically. Positron emission tomography (PET) scan showed decreased splenomegaly from 17 to 15 cm in axial dimension and diminished his diffuse lymphadenopathy. He also responded to ART and his HIV viral load dropped to 40 copies/mL.
Three months later, he became nonadherent to his ART due to heavy alcohol abuse. He was readmitted due to jaundice and fever and found to have elevated bilirubin and transaminases with negative work up for biliary obstruction and bacterial cholangitis. Due to fever, recurrence of pancytopenia and high index of suspicious for recurrence of MCD, he was restarted on another 8 cycles of weekly rituximab followed by doxorubicin liposomal. He was also placed back on his previous ART.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old male presenting with persistent fevers, bilateral flank pain, nausea, and vomiting for five days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 5-day history of persistent high-grade fevers, bilateral flank pain, nausea, and emesis. Three years prior, he experienced a similar syndrome of fever, abdominal pain, pancytopenia, and generalized lymphadenopathy that resolved following compliance with antiretroviral medications. During the current admission, his course was complicated by healthcare-associated diarrhea secondary to Clostridioides difficile colitis, which resolved with oral vancomycin. Three months post-discharge, he developed recurrent fever, jaundice, and cytopenias in the setting of heavy alcohol intake.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underlying chronic retroviral infection diagnosed six years prior, with medication non-adherence for over two years; prior generalized lymphadenopathy and pancytopenia three years prior with non-malignant lymph node biopsies (benign lymphoid hyperplasia) and bone marrow evaluation. Social history: Men who have sex with men (MSM); significant chronic alcohol abuse; denies travel outside the United States or animal exposures.
subjective.review_of_systems: Persistent fevers, bilateral flank and abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea; denies focal cough or dysuria.

objective.physical_examination: Vitals: Body temperature 38.8 °C, blood pressure 161/96 mmHg, pulse rate 145 beats/min (marked tachycardia), respiratory rate 22 breaths/min. Abdomen: Hepatosplenomegaly. Lymphatics: Diffuse, nontender bilateral axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Severe pancytopenia. Inflammatory markers: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Serology & Virology: CMV IgG and Parvovirus B19 IgG positive; CMV DNA PCR and Parvovirus B19 DNA PCR negative; bacterial and fungal blood cultures sterile. Stool testing: Positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin.
objective.advanced_workup: CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis: Marked bilateral diffuse axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy and pronounced hepatosplenomegaly. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy: Normocellular marrow with megakaryocytic hyperplasia, decreased iron stores, absence of acid-fast or fungal pathogens, and no malignancy. Percutaneous core needle biopsy of right inguinal lymph node: Scant non-diagnostic lymphoid fragments. Right inguinal excisional lymph node biopsy: Interfollicular plasma cell sheets and germinal centers with penetrating vascularity and classic concentric 'onion-skin' hyaline-vascular architecture; submitted for specialized immunohistochemical evaluation. Positron emission tomography (PET): Marked diffuse adenopathy and splenic enlargement (17 cm axial diameter), which reduced to 15 cm following therapy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)-associated multicentric Castleman disease (MCD) in a patient with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (CD4+ T-cell count 27 cells/microL [6%], HIV-1 viral load 98,200 copies/mL) complicated by secondary Clostridioides difficile colitis. Diagnostic confirmation: Histopathology of excisional lymph node biopsy demonstrating characteristic hyaline-vascular and plasma-cell features with positive HHV-8 immunostaining, accompanied by extremely high serum HHV-8 DNA quantitative viremia of 2,288,277 copies/mL (reference < 1,000 copies/mL); HIV genotypic testing confirmed no transmissible resistance. Plan & Outcome: Treated for C. difficile colitis with oral vancomycin. Restarted on combination ART with bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (Biktarvy), with viral load dropping to 40 copies/mL. Received 6 cycles of intravenous rituximab leading to clinical resolution, reduction in spleen size, and regression of lymphadenopathy. Following disease flare three months later linked to medication non-adherence, successfully retreated with 8 cycles of weekly rituximab followed by liposomal doxorubicin and re-establishment of ART.
